prompt.task: Act as the second-stage scientist after the first target experiments. Test the frozen transfer hypothesis against only the newly revealed evidence, revise it when needed, and select the next experiments within the fixed budget.

original_hypothesis.hypothesis: Using same-precatalyst transfer, Morpholine-AlPhos will favor high-temperature candidates with moderate base equivalents (~1.1-1.5 or ~2.0) and medium-to-long residence times; therefore at least one of the selected high-temperature candidates should outperform the lower-temperature same-precatalyst quality anchor.
original_hypothesis.mechanism: The most relevant transferred evidence is from AlPhos campaigns. In Aniline-AlPhos, top outcomes cluster at high temperature with moderate base equivalents and mid/long residence times, especially DBU/TMG around feature0 ~0.20-0.28 and feature2 ~0.55-0.61. In Benzamide-AlPhos, absolute performance is lower but useful results still occur at moderate base equivalents and non-extreme conditions, indicating AlPhos tolerates that region across substrates. The target shortlist offers several same-precatalyst-supported BTMG options. Candidate 018 is the best balanced same-precatalyst/high-all-sources option and anchors the likely productive region: BTMG, 100 C, 1.48 eq, long time. Candidate 009 probes lower base equivalents at otherwise similar high-T/long-time conditions, matching the strong AlPhos pattern that moderate-to-low equivalents can still be excellent. Candidate 001 is the highest same-precatalyst score and probes whether a shorter residence time and lower temperature, but similar BTMG loading and ~2 eq base, transfers better to morpholine than the hotter long-time regime. This gives one source-quality anchor plus two plausible probes spanning base equivalent and time/temperature tradeoffs without leaving the source-supported manifold.
failure_conditions: If Morpholine-AlPhos fundamentally prefers a different base identity regime than prior AlPhos substrates, especially BTTP or MTBD over BTMG, this design can miss the optimum.
If morpholine reactivity is much more temperature-sensitive than aniline/benzamide under AlPhos, the 47.5 C probe may underperform and weaken transfer.
If the target optimum requires very short residence time at 100 C rather than medium/long times, candidates 018 and 009 may be too slow.
If same-precatalyst transfer is less informative than broader cross-substrate amine trends, selecting only BTMG candidates may limit early learning.
If the elevated catalyst loading in the target changes the ranking of numeric conditions relative to prior AlPhos campaigns, transferred preferences may not hold.

scientific_context.evidence_boundary: Only the listed initial target outcomes are revealed. Outcomes for all remaining candidates are hidden.

required_output_schema.evidence_interpretation: what the revealed results support and contradict
required_output_schema.next_experiment_rationale: why these experiments are maximally informative

constraints: Select exactly 2 unique IDs from remaining_candidate_shortlist unless stop_transfer=true.
Use only revealed_initial_target_results as target evidence.
Do not infer or invent outcomes for remaining candidates.
Explicitly identify evidence that contradicts the original hypothesis.
Prefer experiments that discriminate between the revised hypothesis and a counter-hypothesis.
Do not change the total experiment budget, GP kernel, or candidate pool.
Stop transfer when the initial evidence falsifies the mechanism or makes source guidance unsafe.

parsed_response.evidence_interpretation: The initial target results show that the high-temperature candidates with moderate base equivalents and long residence times (candidates 018 and 009) yield moderate outcomes (~38-39%), which is lower than the high yields observed in the source AlPhos campaigns with Aniline and Benzamide substrates. The low-temperature candidate 001 with lower temperature and shorter residence time performed poorly (~1.3%). This partially supports the hypothesis that high temperature and moderate base equivalents are favorable, but the absolute yields are much lower than expected from source data, indicating substrate-specific effects. The poor performance of candidate 001 supports the temperature sensitivity aspect. However, the moderate yields of candidates 018 and 009 contradict the expectation that at least one high-temperature candidate would outperform the lower-temperature anchor significantly. This suggests that the transfer of the same-precatalyst high-temperature regime from Aniline/Benzamide to Morpholine is only partially valid and that Morpholine-AlPhos may have different optimal conditions or base preferences.
parsed_response.revised_hypothesis: For Morpholine-AlPhos, moderate base equivalents (~1.1-1.5) and high temperature (~100 C) with long residence times yield moderate product formation, but the maximum achievable yield is lower than in Aniline-AlPhos or Benzamide-AlPhos campaigns. Lower temperature and shorter residence time conditions are suboptimal. The optimal base identity may differ from BTMG, and exploring alternative bases such as BTTP or MTBD could improve yields. Therefore, further exploration of base identity and residence time at high temperature is necessary to identify improved conditions.
parsed_response.next_experiment_rationale: Candidate 013 uses BTTP base at high temperature and short residence time, probing the effect of base identity and shorter residence time at 100 C, which contrasts with the initial BTMG high-temperature long-time candidates. Candidate 022 uses BTMG base at moderate temperature (~75 C) and long residence time, probing the temperature boundary and residence time effect within the same base. These experiments will discriminate whether base identity or temperature/residence time tradeoffs dominate yield improvements, clarifying the revised hypothesis and guiding further optimization.
